questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) What do you understand by the term mineral deposit? (2 marks)

(ii) List the various types of mineral deposits found in Cameroon. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** A **mineral deposit** is a **natural concentration of a useful mineral or rock in the Earth's crust**, greater than the average amount, which may be worth extracting. When it can be mined at a profit it is called an **ore deposit** (an ore).

**(ii) Types of mineral deposits found in Cameroon** (with examples):

- **Metallic minerals:** bauxite (aluminium; e.g. Minim-Martap, Ngaoundal), iron ore (e.g. Mbalam), gold (East Region), cobalt and nickel (e.g. Lomie), rutile (titanium; e.g. Akonolinga), tin (cassiterite).
- **Industrial (non-metallic) minerals and rocks:** limestone (e.g. Figuil), clay, sand, gravel and granite for construction, pozzolan.
- **Gemstones:** diamond (East Region).
- **Fuels:** petroleum and natural gas (e.g. Rio del Rey and Douala basins).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Describe the following sedimentary structures:

(i) Cross bedding. (2 marks)

(ii) Graded bedding. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Cross bedding:** within a bed, thin layers (foresets) are **inclined at an angle to the main bedding planes**, which are horizontal; each set of inclined layers is cut off at the top and bottom by the horizontal planes. It forms when **wind or water currents** move sand as dunes, ripples or delta fronts. The slope of the foresets shows the **direction of the current** (palaeocurrent) and the truncated tops of the sets show the way up. Typical in sandstones.

**(ii) Graded bedding:** a bed in which the **grain size changes gradually from coarse at the bottom to fine at the top**. It forms when a current carrying mixed sediment (typically a **turbidity current**) loses energy, so the coarse grains settle first and the fine ones last. It shows which way up the beds are.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) State the various types of magma. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to silica content, there are three main types of magma:

1. **Basaltic (mafic) magma:** about 45 to 52 % silica; hot and fluid; produces basalt and gabbro.
2. **Andesitic (intermediate) magma:** about 52 to 66 % silica; produces andesite and diorite.
3. **Rhyolitic (granitic, felsic) magma:** more than about 66 % silica; cooler and viscous; produces rhyolite and granite.
